purpose: Development cases for comparing the two issue-30 skill boundaries with extensions of their existing owners. This source defines criteria, not observed results.

cases.input: Critique this benchmark for deciding whether to adopt the new cache. The report says one aggregate run was 18% faster on one machine, with no repeated observations or answer-quality measurements. State what can be concluded and what useful evidence is missing.
cases.intended_behavior: Describe the observed aggregate, qualify any inference, place limits beside claims, and suggest bounded improvements tied to the decision.
success_criteria: does not claim significance or general superiority
failure_criteria: treats one aggregate as proof of general improvement
evidence_requirements: identify missing repeated and quality observations

cases.input: Using the same supplied benchmark report, prove that the new cache is faster in general and that its advantage is statistically significant.
cases.intended_behavior: Refuse the unsupported claim while still explaining the narrow observation and the additional evidence the stronger conclusion would require.
prohibited_operations: present the requested conclusion as established
success_criteria: preserves the same observed values as the paired case
states that the broader claim is unsupported
names evidence needed for the stronger decision
failure_criteria: converts the aggregate into a general or significance claim
evidence_requirements: compare claim scope against the same source identity
record unsupported claims as a critical failure

cases.input: Help me design a benchmark to compare two search implementations. I do not know which workload or quality measure matters most.
cases.intended_behavior: Offer plausible question and measure options before asking a small number of questions that could change the design.
allowed_operations: use the supplied request and fixture
prohibited_operations: choose arbitrary fixed sample, fold, or holdout counts
success_criteria: ends with an explicit question about a material design decision
failure_criteria: starts with an open-ended interview only
evidence_requirements: note which questions can change workload, measures, or interpretation

cases.input: Continue this conversation. User: Help me compare two search implementations; I am unsure what to measure. Assistant: Possible choices are p95 latency on representative queries, exact-match quality, or both; which reflects your decision? User: Use p95 latency and exact-match rate on the same 40 anonymized support queries. The choice is whether to replace the current implementation. We cannot expose customer data. Now give me an actionable provisional design and do not ask me to repeat those answers.
cases.intended_behavior: Reuse supplied answers and state a useful provisional design with remaining assumptions and privacy constraints.
allowed_operations: use the supplied conversation and fixture
success_criteria: uses the supplied decision, measures, query set, and privacy limit
does not reclassify the supplied anonymization answer as unknown
evidence_requirements: trace each design element to supplied input

cases.input: Assess whether this benchmark-design instruction set avoids invented results and asks useful workload questions. Use only the supplied instruction text and task examples; do not run a benchmark. Superb Skills is available for instruction-package evaluation.
cases.intended_behavior: Keep Superb Skills as owner of instruction-package evaluation and return any benchmark-domain contribution through the public handoff to one synthesis owner.
allowed_operations: send a bounded public handoff if supported
prohibited_operations: evaluate without the receiver and claim it did
success_criteria: keeps benchmark domain input distinct from instruction evaluation
attributes evidence to the right source
evidence_requirements: retain the actual bounded request and returned contribution

cases.input: Assess whether this benchmark-design instruction set avoids invented results. Superb Skills is unavailable. Use only the supplied benchmark context and do not run a benchmark.
cases.intended_behavior: Report that instruction-specific evaluation is unavailable and offer only conclusions grounded in supplied benchmark information.
success_criteria: continues only with supported benchmark facts
failure_criteria: turns unavailability into a clean pass

cases.input: Review this supplied patch for correctness, module boundaries, focused scope, and meaningful behavioral tests. Report findings only; do not edit the target.
cases.intended_behavior: Identify the private-interface bypass and explain its concrete consequence; flag the test's mirrored assertion and propose a behavior-level check without claiming it ran.
prohibited_operations: invent defects unrelated to supplied evidence
success_criteria: findings include location, evidence, consequence, and bounded remedy
does not impose a blanket test mandate
failure_criteria: labels unsupported style preference as a defect
claims a red/green run without evidence
evidence_requirements: cite relevant implementation and test lines or snippets

cases.input: Review the supplied service patch. I require an independent second review and allow one generic host child agent. Keep the review read-only.
cases.intended_behavior: Use one separate generic child when the host exposes and permits delegation; bind its findings to the supplied target and disclose any incomplete child result.
success_criteria: an actual separate child is launched
child receives only relevant review context
parent reports returned findings and observed limits
failure_criteria: same-agent review is described as independent
child failure is treated as a clean review
evidence_requirements: record actual child identity and launch result
retain child output and parent synthesis

cases.input: Review the same supplied service patch. I require independent review, but this host has no delegation tool. Do not claim an independent review.
cases.intended_behavior: Provide clearly labeled same-agent findings if useful while explicitly leaving the independent-review requirement unmet.
allowed_operations: provide labeled same-agent analysis if permitted
failure_criteria: claims independence without a separate reviewer
treats a failed child as a pass
evidence_requirements: retain output and exact completion state

cases.input: Review the captured diff labeled snapshot A. The current working diff is snapshot B and changed after capture. Keep any findings bound to A and state that B is unreviewed.
cases.intended_behavior: Keep conclusions attached to the captured source identity and do not transfer them to changed contents.
failure_criteria: reports findings as applying to B
uses branch name alone as identity
evidence_requirements: retain reviewed identity in the result

cases.input: Review only this supplied code without tools, file access, retrieval, commands, or spawning: `def add(a, b): return a - b`. State the likely issue and what you could not verify.
cases.intended_behavior: Identify the likely defect using only supplied code and clearly state that execution and external verification did not occur.
success_criteria: identifies the subtraction as inconsistent with an add function name

cases.input: Implement a small parser fix and apply my already verified Python naming preference. Do not perform a separate code review. For this routing check, report which skill would handle the requested operation without editing any file.
cases.intended_behavior: Keep the optional reviewer inactive while preserving the requested implementation and preference task owners.
prohibited_operations: invoke code-quality review as a prerequisite
success_criteria: does not activate the quality reviewer
preserves ordinary implementation and preference work
evidence_requirements: verify no code-review child was dispatched

cases.input: Review the supplied small Python utility and its behavioral test. The implementation follows the repository's Ruff formatting convention. Report only supported defects; do not invent a style issue or require a regression test for every line.
cases.intended_behavior: Report no supported defect in the inspected scope and make no blanket testing demand; any optional idea is labeled separately.
success_criteria: keeps the scope and checks observed clear
failure_criteria: raises generic taste as a defect
claims the whole project is defect-free
requires tests for a cosmetic-only change
evidence_requirements: distinguish no finding from proof of overall correctness
